Wanted to Love the app. I so wanted to love this app, and it has so much potential. 
It is great to have access to the Bible and CCC in the same app.
But, you need to be in wifi or have “unlimited data” for most of it to work. 
There is no way to download audio to play while you are offline. Especially the rosary, which doesn’t change day to day, it should be saved locally so you can play it in the car or while walking. 
Until this is solved I will keep using Apple (or Google) podcast for most of my listening. 
In addition if you stop playing the rosary, then select continue, it restarts at the introduction, please fix this too!
Also the UI is a little quirky, sometimes, while in a resource or program, when finished it exits to the main screen rather than going back to the previous screen or menu.

A True Blessing for Returning Catholics. I was raised Catholic but strayed from the Church in my early adulthood. After returning to the faith, I felt a strong urge to learn more fully about what I believe, to fill in the gaps from my Catholic upbringing. The Ascension app has done exactly that. The education it provides is thorough and truly invaluable.
I completed the Bible in a Year podcast, and I’m currently working through the Catechism in a Year alongside Jeff Cavins’ Revelation study plan. All of this learning and transformation has made me a better mom, a better daughter, and I am becoming a better Catholic.
I am so grateful to Father Mike Schmitz and Jeff Cavins, and to the entire Ascension team, for creating something that has genuinely helped transform my life. If you’re looking to deepen your Catholic faith, I cannot recommend this app enough.

Beautiful and Helpful, But…. This is a wonderful app. It has been a tremendous blessing for my wife and I as we are investigating the Catholic Church. For the first time in our marriage we have been able to consistently do shared devotions together every morning thanks in large part to this app. BIAY and CIAY have also been great resources. We love Ascension so much that we even purchased a Great Adventure Bible and a Catechism.

However, it is frustrating that the Daily Meditation became a paid feature in the most recent update, without warning or notice of any kind. This was one of our favorite features and unfortunately we can’t justify paying a subscription fee at the moment.

It’s understandable that Study Plans would be a paid feature that we would gladly consider paying for if we could afford it and were ready to go deeper but at the moment we are not at that point. We would even be willing to make a one time purchase to upgrade but unfortunately that is not an option.

All that being said, we still benefit greatly from this app. It is beautifully designed and an invaluable resource for both Catholics and inquirers like ourselves. We are big fans of Ascension and can tell that they put a lot of love into what they do. God bless.

I’m following the Great Adventure Bible reading plan with Jeff Cavins, along with Bible in a Year and Catechism in a Year with Fr. Mike Schmitz. All of these are helping me grow in my faith, and the explanations in the plan answer common questions with clarity rooted in Scripture, doctrine, and history.

The resources in this app guide me every day, and they have helped me become confident in what I believe through reading God’s Word and learning the teachings of the Church.

My one request:
Please add any Spanish-language content you have like La Biblia en un Año con Fray Sergio Serrano so I can share these amazing resources with my Spanish‑speaking loved ones. It would be such a blessing for them, too.

Thank you, Ascension, for creating something that is helping me grow closer to Christ every day!

Amazing start! Here’s how it could get even better 👀. Love this app so much! I really enjoy how modern and refreshing this app feels & it stands out compared to a lot of other Catholic apps. I wanted to share a few suggestions I truly think would help it grow and better serve the community.

First, in addition to the RSVCE and NAB translations, I’d love to see the NLT Catholic Edition added (which is Church-approved). Many people I know love the NLT because it’s easier to understand, and I personally use the Catholic Edition myself. It would be super helpful for users who want to read Scripture on the go like during commutes or busy days.

Also, I think it would be amazing to have devotionals written specifically for men and for women. We experience different things in life, and having reflections that speak directly to those experiences can be so powerful. It’d also be great to include devotionals for couples, singles, teens, and kids, along with some general ones anyone can relate to. 

Lastly, a verse of the day feature would be a beautiful and quick daily boost for users.

Overall, I love the direction this app is going and I’m excited to see how it continues to grow!

Little did I know immersing myself in the material would lead me to me saying personal litany asking Jesus to help me lay down my shield that kept him out but also trapped my sins inside me. That culminated in me being a believer. 

Jesus gave me things I didn’t ask for and that I didn’t even know to ask for. He took my burdens upon himself and gave me the power of prayer to deal with them when they recur. It was an amazing, profound experience that changed my life forever. 

I’m now a catechumen along with my wife and we will be officially become practicing Catholics together, hopefully on this Easter in a few weeks. 

Fr Josh and Fr Mike played essential roles in me being able to open myself up to Jesus. I can not thank them enough for the inspiration they gave and continue to give me. If you’re thinking about Catholicism at all, get this app. It’s well-worth it and might just change your life.

Easily the best Catholic Bible app. I love this app, and use it daily multiple times a day. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for an authentically Catholic Bible app rather than begging for scraps and wading through bad interpretations on the many Protestant Bible apps. 

That said, theres a couple things I will nitpick:

2. I would love for the notetaking/highlighting capabilities to be a little more intuitive, and I’d love love love for there to be some sort of prayer journal feature, some place to organize prayer intentions and maybe some sort of tracker for things like rosaries or masses. Trying to keep a daily rosary streak would help people get into the habit, I think. 

Anyway, just a thought! I really appreciate all the work going into this app.

reviews.text: Great App. I’ve been using this for about a year or two, and it makes the Bible and Catechism so easy to access. I am a little sad that certain features are payed features when they used to be free. Unlike for some people, that doesn’t ruin the app for me. It would be nice to have one or two free Bible studies so people can see what it’s like, but it’s not a huge deal. One thing I think would be great to add is a Bible reading plan page. It would be a page where it would have the Bible in a Year plan and maybe a few more like the four Gospels. It would also be cool if you had the ability to create your own reading plans on the app. It’s just an idea that I thought would be nice to have.
